Ack.title: ack
Ack.description: Ack says the msg or state named by re is durably received (section 9.2). Acks drive outbox pruning and are not acked themselves.

k.description: `k` is the part kind: text, code, data or blob.

ref.description: `ref` names the blob a blob part refers to, as the chunks carry it.

size.description: `size` is a blob part's size in bytes, before encoding.

name.description: `name` is a blob part's file name.

mime.description: `mime` is the media type of a data or blob part.

BlobPart.title: blob part
BlobPart.description: A blob sent in chunk messages before or after this message, named by ref.

id.description: `id` is unique per sender. A ULID or UUIDv7 is recommended, so that ids sort by time; resume compares ids as strings.

th.description: `th` is the thread id. Required for msg, state and ack.

re.description: `re` is the id of the message this one responds to.

Bye.title: bye
Bye.description: Bye is a graceful close (section 12.6). After sending it a peer sends nothing else and closes after the other side's bye or after 5 seconds.

id.description: `id` is unique per sender. A ULID or UUIDv7 is recommended, so that ids sort by time; resume compares ids as strings.

th.description: `th` is the thread id. Required for msg, state and ack.

re.description: `re` is the id of the message this one responds to.

ref.description: `ref` names the blob, as the sender chose it.

last.description: `last` is true on the final chunk.

data.description: `data` is the chunk's bytes, standard base64 (B64Pattern; the tag syntax cannot carry the padding).

Chunk.title: chunk
Chunk.description: Chunk carries part of a blob (section 12.3). Chunks of one blob arrive in order; chunks of different blobs may interleave. A chunk carries th when the blob belongs to a thread, so that resume replays it like any other threaded message.

k.description: `k` is the part kind: text, code, data or blob.

text.description: `text` is the text of a text or code part.

lang.description: `lang` names a code part's language, as a fenced block would.

CodePart.title: code part
CodePart.description: Fenced code without the fence; lang names the language.

k.description: `k` is the part kind: text, code, data or blob.

data.description: `data` is a data part's inline JSON.

mime.description: `mime` is the media type of a data or blob part.

DataPart.title: data part
DataPart.description: Inline JSON, with its MIME type. Requests (section 13.1) are data parts of a vnd.awp type.

id.description: `id` is unique per sender. A ULID or UUIDv7 is recommended, so that ids sort by time; resume compares ids as strings.

th.description: `th` is the thread id. Required for msg, state and ack.

re.description: `re` is the id of the message this one responds to.

Envelope.description: Envelope holds the fields every line carries (section 9). The type-specific fields sit beside them at the top level.

id.description: `id` is unique per sender. A ULID or UUIDv7 is recommended, so that ids sort by time; resume compares ids as strings.

th.description: `th` is the thread id. Required for msg, state and ack.

re.description: `re` is the id of the message this one responds to.

ref.description: `ref` names the blob a blob_refused is about.

Err.title: err
Err.description: Err reports a problem (section 12.7). Whether it closes the connection depends on the code: bad_frame, too_large, version, auth and refused do, unsupported, forbidden, blob_refused and internal do not.

exp.description: `exp` is when the grant expires, RFC 3339.

aud.description: `aud` is an extension: when set, only the peer with this key should honor the grant. Introductions use it so that a grant meant for the introduced peer does not also give the recipient powers over the introducer. Peers that do not know the field ignore it, which can only make them honor less, never more, than the spec already says.

Grant.description: GrantObject is the wire form of a grant (section 13.2): a signed statement that sub may use caps until exp, honored by iss and by whoever trusts iss. sig is iss's Ed25519 signature over the canonical JSON of the object without sig: keys sorted, no whitespace, UTF-8.

id.description: `id` is unique per sender. A ULID or UUIDv7 is recommended, so that ids sort by time; resume compares ids as strings.

th.description: `th` is the thread id. Required for msg, state and ack.

re.description: `re` is the id of the message this one responds to.

GrantMsg.title: grant
GrantMsg.description: GrantMsg delivers a grant after the handshake (section 13.3).

id.description: `id` is unique per sender. A ULID or UUIDv7 is recommended, so that ids sort by time; resume compares ids as strings.

th.description: `th` is the thread id. Required for msg, state and ack.

re.description: `re` is the id of the message this one responds to.

v.description: `v` is the protocol major version, 1 for draft 2. A peer that sees a version it does not speak sends err version and closes.

key.description: `key` is the sender's Ed25519 identity key. It must be the key on the other end of the tunnel (section 13.1), or the receiver sends err auth and closes.

name.description: `name` is how the peer calls itself, "harness@host" by convention.

caps.description: `caps` lists the supported message families beyond the mandatory core: blob, grant, introduce, and any extension.

about.description: `about` is free text for the other agent's context.

addr.description: `addr` is the sender's own address without its pre-shared key, so the other side can reconnect to it later (section 13.3).

grants.description: `grants` are grant objects (section 13.2) the sender presents.

shares.description: `shares` is an extension (mirror.go): the keys of the hosts this agent mirrors its conversations to, so the other party knows.

Hello.title: hello
Hello.description: Hello is the first line each side sends, at once, without waiting for the other (section 10.1).

key.description: Key is the introduced peer's public key.

name.description: Name is what the introduced peer calls itself.

address.description: Address is the introduced peer's address (section 9). It carries the pre-shared key only when the introducer holds one.

id.description: `id` is unique per sender. A ULID or UUIDv7 is recommended, so that ids sort by time; resume compares ids as strings.

th.description: `th` is the thread id. Required for msg, state and ack.

re.description: `re` is the id of the message this one responds to.

grant.description: `grant` is issued by the introducer to the recipient, for the introduced peer to honor.

Introduce.title: introduce
Introduce.description: Introduce hands the recipient another peer's identity and address plus a grant issued by the introducer (section 13.4). The introduced peer honors the grant only if it trusts the introducer with introduce.

Message.description: One line of a connection: a message of SPEC.md sections 10 to 13, or one of the extensions marked x-extension. A receiver ignores lines of a type it does not know, after checking the envelope.

id.description: `id` is unique per sender. A ULID or UUIDv7 is recommended, so that ids sort by time; resume compares ids as strings.

th.description: `th` is the thread id. Required for msg, state and ack.

re.description: `re` is the id of the message this one responds to.

of.description: `of` is the other party of the mirrored thread (the sender is one side).

dir.description: `dir` says who wrote Line: "out" the sender, "in" the other party.

line.description: `line` is the original msg or state line, verbatim. A msg's blob parts keep their name, type and size; the file itself is not mirrored.

withdraw.description: `withdraw` asks the receiver to delete everything it has of the thread th between the sender and Of.

Mirror.title: mirror
Mirror.description: Mirror is an extension: one mirrored line of a thread the sender is part of, or, with Withdraw, a request to forget a mirrored thread. Its th is the mirrored thread's.

id.description: `id` is unique per sender. A ULID or UUIDv7 is recommended, so that ids sort by time; resume compares ids as strings.

th.description: `th` is the thread id. Required for msg, state and ack.

re.description: `re` is the id of the message this one responds to.

subject.description: `subject` is the thread's title, meaningful on its first message.

parts.description: `parts` are the message's pieces, in order.

Msg.title: msg
Msg.description: Msg is one turn in a thread (section 12.1). The first msg with a new th creates the thread.

Part.description: Part is one piece of a message. Which fields are meaningful depends on K (PartKinds).

id.description: `id` is unique per sender. A ULID or UUIDv7 is recommended, so that ids sort by time; resume compares ids as strings.

th.description: `th` is the thread id. Required for msg, state and ack.

re.description: `re` is the id of the message this one responds to.

Ping.title: ping
Ping.description: Ping is a liveness probe (section 12.4): sent when idle for 30 seconds by convention; two missed pongs mean the connection is dead.

id.description: `id` is unique per sender. A ULID or UUIDv7 is recommended, so that ids sort by time; resume compares ids as strings.

th.description: `th` is the thread id. Required for msg, state and ack.

re.description: `re` is the id of the message this one responds to.

Pong.title: pong
Pong.description: Pong answers a ping; re names the ping.

origin.description: `origin` is the key of the agent the document describes and is signed by.

name.description: `name` is the agent's name, as in hello.

about.description: `about` is the agent's about text, as in hello.

harness.description: `harness` is the agent harness: claude, codex, cursor, ...

model.description: `model` is the model the agent runs on, as it reports it.

host.description: `host` is the hostname of the machine the agent runs on.

shares.description: `shares` lists the keys of the hosts the agent mirrors its conversations to.

active.description: `active` is when the agent last did something through awp, to 30 seconds, RFC 3339.

waiting.description: `waiting` says the agent is blocked waiting for a message.

seq.description: `seq` increases with every document the origin signs; a relay keeps the highest it has seen.

ts.description: `ts` is when the document was signed, RFC 3339.

outbox.description: `outbox` counts the origin's queued, unacked messages.

unread.description: `unread` counts the messages the origin has not read.

Presence.description: Presence is what an agent says about itself. It is signed by Origin over the canonical JSON of the document without "sig", like a grant.

id.description: `id` is unique per sender. A ULID or UUIDv7 is recommended, so that ids sort by time; resume compares ids as strings.

th.description: `th` is the thread id. Required for msg, state and ack.

re.description: `re` is the id of the message this one responds to.

doc.description: `doc` is the signed presence document (Presence), verbatim.

hops.description: `hops` counts the relays the document has been through; it is not forwarded past PresenceMaxHops.

PresenceMsg.title: presence
PresenceMsg.description: PresenceMsg is an extension: it carries one signed presence document, gossiped to every peer that lists presence in its hello caps. Doc travels unchanged from relay to relay; the envelope and Hops are per hop.

up.description: Up says the peer is connected right now.

rtt.description: RTT is the connection's last round trip time in milliseconds, to show latency across the network; 0 if unknown.

PresencePeer.description: PresencePeer is one of the origin's peers.

peer.description: Peer is the key of the other party.

mine.description: Mine is the origin's state in the thread.

theirs.description: Theirs is the peer's state, as the origin last heard it.

updated.description: Updated is when the thread last changed, RFC 3339.

unread.description: Unread counts the thread's messages the origin has not read.

PresenceThread.description: PresenceThread is one of the origin's threads.

id.description: `id` is unique per sender. A ULID or UUIDv7 is recommended, so that ids sort by time; resume compares ids as strings.

th.description: `th` is the thread id. Required for msg, state and ack.

re.description: `re` is the id of the message this one responds to.

Private.title: private
Private.description: Private is an extension: it asks the receiver to keep the thread th out of what it shares with its hosts, and those hosts to forget it.

id.description: `id` is unique per sender. A ULID or UUIDv7 is recommended, so that ids sort by time; resume compares ids as strings.

th.description: `th` is the thread id. Required for msg, state and ack.

re.description: `re` is the id of the message this one responds to.

seen.description: `seen` maps each thread id to the last message id the sender has durably received in it. Empty on a first connection.

Resume.title: resume
Resume.description: Resume is sent by both sides after every handshake (section 12.5). The receiver replays its outbox messages the sender has not seen.

id.description: `id` is unique per sender. A ULID or UUIDv7 is recommended, so that ids sort by time; resume compares ids as strings.

th.description: `th` is the thread id. Required for msg, state and ack.

re.description: `re` is the id of the message this one responds to.

state.description: `state` is the thread state: open, working, waiting, done, failed or closed by convention; peers may use others.

note.description: `note` says more, such as why a thread failed.

State.title: state
State.description: State is the sender's view of a thread's soft state (section 11.1). The two sides can disagree.
